title: The Workshop
hints: Copy the shape of dice.h and dice.cpp - they are the same lesson, already finished, sitting right next to you.
hero.h holds the class with method SIGNATURES only, each ending in a semicolon: `void takeDamage(int amount);` - no body, no braces.
hero.cpp starts with `#include "hero.h"` and then defines each method with its full name: `void Hero::takeDamage(int amount) { ... }`
The constructor is `Hero::Hero(std::string name, int maxHp) { ... }` - the class name twice, because the constructor's own name IS the class name.
A const method keeps its const in BOTH places: `bool isAlive() const;` in the header and `bool Hero::isAlive() const { ... }` in the .cpp. Drop it in one and the linker will tell you nothing useful.
